delivery.offline: after assets are cached; not yet guaranteed

notes: This is an experimental browser prototype, not a production game release.
N-BI consumes 10 Mana per successful Chaos shot in the current prototype; upgrade-based cost reduction is not yet implemented.
No server account or cloud save exists.
Random game is selected on each fresh launch; a running round stays fixed until ended or page reload.
Generation 1.4 adds an independent 320x180 pixel-art city layer with local dawn/day/dusk/night phases and reduced-motion handling.
The adaptive runtime file remains unchanged; pixel-world quality is adjusted after the existing calibration.
Pixel skyline is procedural placeholder art and is not yet a canonical, source-confirmed Niroo City illustration.
Generation 1.5 expands the renderer into a layered, source-neutral landscape with a moving sun arc, night-only stars, river, forest, coast, fields, city terraces and distant traffic.
Mouse camera follows pointer after first mouse movement; touch camera activates after first touch gesture and uses inverse drag. Drag gestures are excluded from game interactions.
Chaos targets now advance toward the defensive boundary; each unneutralized mass causes one HP damage and is removed. A successful N-BI interaction neutralizes one mass.
Generation 1.5 adds separate mouse-follow and inverse touch-drag camera input; drag gestures are excluded from gameplay interactions.
Unneutralized Chaos masses move toward the defensive boundary; each mass crossing causes one HP damage and then disappears.
Niroo City terrain geography in the renderer is a non-canonical visual proposal based on published urban descriptions; see NU-WORLD-VISUAL-BIBLE-G1.5.md.

pixelWorld.timeCycle: local dawn/day/dusk/night; stars only at night
layers: desert ridges, forest belt and tropical coast
depth-scaled city skyline and green terraces

weatherModes.game: radial particles fast near center and decelerating toward edges

pixelWorld.reducedMotion: static scene; redraw only on time phase changes
